name: 10-roomlight-20260816
incident: cam-H 2026-08-16 (live test, fixed by DN_RATCHET_MARGIN + min_smooth_since_probe)
description:
The everyday event this subsystem exists for, and could not see: someone turns a room light on. Live-observed on cam-H (sc2336, 192.168.1.100) by polling the raw sensor register while flipping the switch. The sensor saw it perfectly - analog gain 85 -> 100 when the light went off, 100 -> 90 -> 86 when it came back on, each edge reached in ~5s and then held flat - which is total_gain 1614 -> 2233 -> 1649 (32 log2 units per stop, so a 15-unit register move is a 38% total_gain move, not a 15% one). The decision logic did not react to either edge in any way: no baseline-drift line, no brightening hold, no suspension, no probe. Not for 95s of watching, and - the point of this scenario - not for the next eleven hours either.

The shape, reconstructed from the camera's own syslog. A periodic reconfirm at 23:12 found genuine night and froze the anchor at 1653, which is simply where this room RESTS at night; the backoff went to x4, next probe 03:12. At 23:21 the gain reached 1599, under the 0.97 bar - the trend suspension fired and pulled the deadline in to 00:12. Then the room dimmed on its own to ~2024, the suspension's predicate went false, and the four hours came straight back: the evidence had been measured and then discarded. When the light finally came on it landed at 1649, which is 3% ABOVE the 1603 anchor bar and 66% above the 992 ratchet bar (the ratchet borrowed day_gain_pct=60, an IR-cut-scale threshold, so it demanded analog gain 62 from a room that lives between 85 and 100 - a bar below the whole scene's nightly range, clearing the 256 floor comfortably enough that dn_bar_reachable had nothing to say). Every fast path shut, and the skip gate would then have skipped the 03:12 and 07:12 deadlines on the same 3% margin, leaving probe_max_skip_s at 11:12 as the only recovery.

WHAT THIS SCENARIO DISCRIMINATES, measured both ways against the same tree (harness advice: revert the fix hunks in a copy of the CURRENT build, never build the old tree - the clock contract has to stay). PRE-FIX the machine probes twice down the transient dip and then never leaves night: 4 board switches, mode@3500 and mode@5900 both come back night, and the wrong-mode run is 3100s, ended only by the end of the run. probe_max_skip_s is deliberately left at its 43200 default so it cannot quietly rescue the scene the way a lowered bound would - the pre-fix build has NO recovery inside this scenario at all, which is the finding. POST-FIX the dip at t=1200-1650 is latched in min_smooth_since_probe and survives the room dimming again, so the reconfirm keeps landing one un-backed-off interval after arming instead of four, and the light-on is judged against an anchor that is still live: 7 switches, day at t=3089 (489s after the light, inside one night_reconfirm_s), wrong-mode 189s.

The log assertion that actually separates the two builds is the third one. 'ratchet anchor overrides baseline evidence' alone does NOT - the pre-fix build emits it too, at the t=1285 probe, because there the brightening happens to still be present at the instant the deadline comes due. The discriminating line is the one where the minimum and the current reading disagree: 'gain 1513 (lowest since the last probe; now 2409)'. A schedule that reads the instantaneous gain cannot print that line, because it is acting on evidence the current reading no longer shows - which is the whole defect, stated as a log regex.

THE THIRD GATE (added 2026-08-16, after this scenario first passed). With the two fixes above the mode recovered - but at t=3089, 489s after the light, via the periodic reconfirm. The ~30s sustained-brightening path that exists precisely for this event never fired, and tracing the replay tick by tick showed why: the hold's bar is (100+pct)/200 of the LIVE baseline, and the baseline drifts toward smooth_tg. The bar it has to clear is only 22.4% away and DN_BASELINE_ALPHA closes 22.4% in about 25s, against a 30s confirm - so the debounce loses the race by construction. Measured here: at the instant the step completed the margin test was 2.2% short and falling, so it never opened on any tick; 25s later the bar had dropped THROUGH smooth_tg, taking the `>= bar` branch, which re-arms and clears the hold. A permanently brighter room read as 'nothing has changed' from then on. Not slow - erased. brighten_ref freezes the reference while the scene is still at rest and the fast path fires: day at t=2685, 35s after the light-on completes, against t=3089 without it - the gate-3-reverted build fails mode@2750 and runs 353s of wrong mode here.

What that fix does NOT claim, checked by sweeping the step size: a fast, large light-on from a settled dark room (2400 -> 1750, 27%, over 10s) was already caught by the hold before the freeze - both builds switch at t=2644. The freeze WIDENS the catchable band rather than creating it, and the band it adds is exactly where real room lights live: steps close enough to the bar that a few percent of reference contamination decides the outcome. This scenario's 2400 -> 1850 over 50s sits in that band on purpose. The freeze also has to be released again once the reference goes stale, or it walks fad4f40's probe volley down a dawn ramp - scenario 09 caught that immediately (14 switches against a budget of 9) and DN_HOLD_REF_LEAD is the bound; see the two 'cam-H B3' cases in corpus entry 00, which fail in opposite directions.

DN_RATCHET_MARGIN is not asserted by mode here and is not meant to be; with the frozen reference in place the hold's own bar (0.776x ref) is stricter than the ratchet (0.84x anchor), so the ratchet is not the binding gate on this trajectory. It is pinned by name in the property test instead, which is where a claim about whether a bar is reachable belongs.

night_reconfirm_s is compressed to 900s for runtime, which makes the probe cadence look four times busier than the 3600s default this camera actually runs; the bound the click budget is really checking is 'never more often than the un-backed-off schedule', and all nine pre-existing scenarios keep their exact pre-fix switch counts. The light-on step is 2400 -> 1850 (23%, i.e. 12 analog units against the incident's 14) and the transient dip is 1620 -> 1520 (6%, against the incident's 3.3%). Both are a little deeper than the real thing on purpose: the real margins sit inside the smoothed AGC noise band, so replaying them literally would assert on float luck at the bar rather than on whether the schedule LATCHES the evidence, which is the actual defect. RESTATED 2026-08-17: five log assertions on the anchor-override, trend-suspension and sustained-brightening machinery, all gone with the machinery. What replaces them is worth stating precisely, because the first attempt at restating them was wrong: this room light moves the night pipeline 2400 -> 1810, a 25% fall, which is deliberately BELOW path C's one-stop bar (probe_jump_pct=50) - the same threshold that makes headlights and AGC drift free. So path C must NOT fire here (forbidden above) and the heartbeat is what recovers it, 63s later. That is the same division of labour scenario 11 asserts at a smaller magnitude, and asserting it at both ends is what keeps the bar itself from drifting. Every behavioural bound is unchanged and passing: 5 switches against a budget of 8, 9s longest wrong-mode run against 120s.
